data.title: Maryam and the Boat

premise.hero_want: Maryam wants to make her drawing of a boat float.
premise.problem: Her drawing is on a flat sheet, not in the shape of a boat.
premise.mechanism: Maryam leads Mum in folding the sheet into a paper boat, then sets it on water in a bowl.
premise.resolution: The paper boat floats while real boats sail past on the Nile.

pages.text: I sit in the shade with Mum. I look at the Nile boats.
pages.scene: On one shaded balcony, Maryam sits beside Mum and looks over the Nile bank. White felucca boats with tall sails glide past; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: I like to draw each boat. I draw one on a sheet.
pages.scene: Still on the balcony, Maryam draws a simple boat on the cream sheet with a plain graphite pencil. Mum watches; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: I want my boat to float. But a flat sheet is not a boat.
pages.scene: Maryam holds up the same flat sheet and studies her boat drawing. The Nile and its felucca boats remain behind her; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: I have a plan. “Mum, can we make it into a boat?”
pages.scene: Maryam points to the drawing and turns to Mum with an eager smile. They remain seated together in the balcony shade; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: I bend the sheet, and Mum bends it with me. It looks like a boat!
pages.scene: Maryam leads as she and Mum fold the same sheet together, sharing the step on the same page. The finished shape is a simple paper boat; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: Mum has a wide bowl. We fill it.
pages.scene: The wide blue bowl now rests on the balcony floor with clear water inside. Maryam and Mum kneel beside it, with the paper boat nearby; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: I set my boat in the bowl. It floats!
pages.scene: Maryam carefully sets the paper boat on the water while Mum stays beside her. The boat floats in the centre of the blue bowl; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: My boat can float! I smile as Nile boats sail by.
pages.scene: Maryam smiles at her floating paper boat while Mum smiles beside her. Beyond the shaded balcony, felucca boats sail along the Nile; all visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

data.cold_read: The story passes the blocking checks: it is coherent, safe, decodable, driven by Maryam and limited to one adult, two key objects and one simple mechanism. A few lines feel more like captions than a child speaking, and page 6 describes filling the bowl while the scene only shows it already filled. These are minor editorial fixes, not rewrite issues.

issues.detail: “I like to draw each boat” sounds stiff and suggests Maryam draws every boat. “I like to draw boats” is more natural.
“A flat sheet is not a boat” and the repeated “bend/bends” construction are caption-like. Simpler phrasing keeps the same action and phonics level.
The text says the bowl is being filled, but the scene only shows it after filling. Changing the text to Mum setting down the prepared bowl gives the illustrator one clear moment.
